3.0.s.en: (1) The salvation of the Gentiles through Paul

3.0.0.en: Because the door of faith was opened to the Gentiles and St. Paul the Apostle carried this call to them, he became a prisoner, imprisoned in Rome for the sake of Christ and for the sake of preaching to them.

3.1.0.en: God declared His will to Paul by His divine dispensation twice: the first when Christ appeared to him in a great light on the road to Damascus (Acts 9:4-6), and the second when He appeared to him in the temple while he was praying, saying to him, "Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles" (Acts 22:6-21). In this dispensation we see God's wise plan to call the Gentiles to salvation.

3.2.0.en: The mystery: the salvation of the Gentiles like the salvation of the Jews.

3.2.1.en: Here he refers to the earlier revelations that qualified him to be an apostle and made known to him what cannot be known except by revelation, namely that he should proclaim the Gospel among the Gentiles, as he had written before that the call is addressed to both Jews and Gentiles, and that both groups have become members of one Church, bound together by faith and love.

3.3.0.en: As I wrote afore: what Paul wrote earlier, briefly, about Christ the Savior of the Gentiles.

3.3.1.en: When you read what came before in this epistle, you will be able to understand my deep knowledge of the mystery of Christ through divine revelation, and you will have gained understanding and enlightenment to grasp this mystery, which is the acceptance of the Gentiles into the faith.

3.4.0.en: In the generations before the coming of Christ the sons of men did not know of this mystery, which was revealed to Paul and to the rest of the Apostles and prophets in the New Testament after the descent of the Holy Spirit, although there are some hints in the Old Testament, such as "Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people" (Deut 32:43), "in him shall the Gentiles trust" (Rom 15:12, Isa 11:10).

3.5.0.en: Here St. Paul the Apostle shows that the mystery of Christ is that the Gentiles share with the Jews in the blessings of the Kingdom of Christ, and that the Gentiles who became Christians are equal with the Jews who became Christians in the rights of spiritual inheritance and in being members of the body whose head is Christ, and that the promise of redemption, which was given to Adam and Eve and repeated to Abraham and the prophets of the Old Testament, has a share in it for the Gentiles just like the Jews. This is in Christ, that is, by union with Christ, which is the only condition for the Gentiles' sharing with the Jews in the blessings of redemption, and the Gospel is the means of their union with Christ.

3.5.1.en: God's love and arms are open to all people, that everyone who believes in Him and lives in His Church may be saved. So let your heart be open with love to everyone, however far away or however much he rejects God. Pray for him and offer him your love, for God is able to change him, even after a while.

3.6.0.en: Whereof: the Gospel, that is, preaching to the Gentiles.

3.6.1.en: The ministry of the Gospel is the work that God appointed for him, and in the estimation of St. Paul the Apostle this commission is a great gift and a great blessing that God granted him. Thus it is not a favor from himself or because of any personal competence in him, but the divine gift gave him mighty power to preach the Gospel.

3.7.0.en: Here St. Paul the Apostle humbles himself and says that he was not worthy to be an apostle and that he was the least of all the believers in the early Church, yet this great grace was given to him, to preach among the Gentiles the riches of Christ, that is, His wisdom, His holiness and His accomplishing salvation for the sons of men. These are riches the human mind cannot imagine the greatness of or fully grasp the truth of, because the Jews did not imagine that there was salvation for the Gentiles who were far from God.

3.8.0.en: The fellowship of the mystery which from the beginning of the world hath been hid: that is, the Gentiles' sharing with the Jews in salvation. This mystery was hidden in the heart of God and the prophets pointed to it, then it was revealed by Christ the Redeemer. In the Greek text of the Gospel it reads "the dispensation of the mystery" instead of "fellowship", and it means God's plan for the salvation of the Gentiles together with the Jews.

3.8.1.en: Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles, was granted by the grace of God to enlighten the minds of all the sons of men and teach them that the salvation of Christ is shared by the Gentiles with the Jews. This was in the heart of God from eternity, and He declared it plainly in the New Testament by the incarnation of His only-begotten Son and His redemption of mankind.

3.9.0.en: Principalities and powers: some orders of angels.

3.9.1.en: The manifold wisdom of God: that is, the wisdom that ordered the salvation of the Jews by their holding to the Law and the commandments that speak of the Messiah, and the salvation of the Gentiles by repentance from their sins and faith in Christ. God's purpose in preaching the mystery of redemption to the Gentiles is to enlighten all people concerning that mystery, not only human beings but also the angels of heaven, who have authority and great standing, when they see this mystery fulfilled in the one Church, as they see the Gentiles having become members of the body of Christ. Thus God showed His wisdom by the incarnation of Christ and by guiding people to faith according to God's eternal plan, which was fulfilled by the incarnation of His Son, His death and His resurrection.

3.10.0.en: By Christ Jesus we have boldness to draw near to God, confident with assurance that He accepts us as His children by adoption, and that is by our faith in Christ and our union with Him.

3.10.1.en: Is it fitting that the angels rejoice at our salvation and we do not rejoice? ... You can enjoy this joy when you thank God every day for His salvation and His gifts to you, then strive for works of goodness and mercy, keeping away from sources of evil.

3.11.s.en: (3) The Apostle's prayer to strengthen their faith

3.11.0.en: St. Paul the Apostle speaks from within his prison in Rome and says to the people of Ephesus: You should not be weakened because of the sufferings and tribulations I am now undergoing, whether imprisonment, beatings or insults, but we should rejoice in sufferings for the sake of preaching, for these sufferings have become glory for man after having been disgrace and shame.

3.12.0.en: So that the people of Ephesus may not be weakened, St. Paul the Apostle declares that he prays for them with all humility and fervor in petition, with prostration and contrition before God, who is the source of all life for all beings of every kind, whether these beings are angels of their various orders or the families of men everywhere on the face of the earth, of their various races.

3.13.0.en: Strengthened with might: the Holy Spirit supports you and establishes you.

3.13.1.en: The inner man: the human spirit.

3.13.2.en: The essential petition in Paul's prayer is that God glorify them and distinguish them from the rest of mankind by His generous giving, in the work of His Holy Spirit within them.

3.14.0.en: That Christ may dwell permanently in the heart, and where Christ dwells by His Spirit, spiritual life and divine knowledge arise. By faith we are assured of His presence, we accept Him, we trust His promises and we hold fast to Him for salvation.

3.14.1.en: Take care to pray for all those around you, especially when they are troubled or stumbling, and continue your prayers and tears and prostrations, even your fasts, for them, until God lifts from them the warfare of the devil and they overcome and rejoice.

3.15.s.en: (4) The love and power of Christ

3.15.0.en: The breadth: the extent of love so as to include all the Gentiles on the face of the earth.

3.15.1.en: The length: all people in all ages until the end of the world.

3.15.2.en: The depth: love's lifting of people out of the depths of evil and corruption to give them the salvation of Christ. The height: raising people to heaven to enjoy eternal glory.

3.15.3.en: With the support of the Holy Spirit and the dwelling of Christ in you, you will be established in the love of God with the rest of the believers and you will comprehend the dimensions of this love.

3.16.0.en: Which passeth knowledge: surpasses the grasp of the human mind.

3.16.1.en: The fullness of God: the perfection of God.

3.16.2.en: The love of Christ for us passes knowledge; as human beings we cannot grasp it fully, but the believers must advance little by little in comprehending the love of Christ as far as they are able.

3.17.0.en: The power that worketh in us: the power of the Holy Spirit.

3.17.1.en: The Lord has done more than we ask or think; God's generosity is not confined to the limits of our requests or our notions of what we need. There is no limit to the abundance of blessings granted to those in whose hearts Christ dwells by His Holy Spirit.

3.18.0.en: God is glorified in the Church, His bride, in whom that glory is manifested, and she in turn is glorified by Christ her head in all times and in eternity. Amen, that is, let what he has asked be fulfilled, and he calls on all the readers of the epistle to agree with him in that.

3.18.1.en: We have an open account with God to receive many blessings, which we must ask for and work for with all faith and patience, so that we deepen every day and grasp His love through prayer and thanksgiving, and likewise through loving others and striving for their salvation.

3.18.2.en: Renewal, Christian conduct and steadfastness in it

4.0.0.en: Paul calls the believers to hold fast to the commandments of God that he preached to them. He describes himself as a prisoner in the Lord because he is not distressed by prison but accepts it for the sake of Christ. And more than this, he feels joy that he suffers and is bound for His sake, and this joy leads him to hold fast to God's commandments, so that his heart is moved to call all the believers to hold fast with him to God's commandments.

4.0.1.en: Hold fast to God's commandments however hard your circumstances, like Paul's circumstances in prison. Do not seek excuses for yourself and so fall into sin, but ask for God's help and you will see Him before you supporting you, like Joseph who refused sin and endured being thrown into prison, and so was raised to the throne of Egypt.

4.1.0.en: Lowliness: a person feels he is less than everyone, yet by God's grace he lives and is distinguished as well. Meekness: quietness of heart.

4.1.1.en: Longsuffering: good listening and gentleness toward others, whatever their faults.

4.1.2.en: Christian conduct with others depends on humility, quietness of heart and longsuffering, so that a person is able in love to bear the faults of others.

4.2.0.en: Because the Holy Spirit has united the believers in the body of Christ, that is, the Church, we must preserve this unity by making peace with others as far as we can, giving up material things and some rights.

4.2.1.en: The Coptic Church, inspired by the Holy Spirit, placed this text at the beginning of the prayer of Prime in the Agpeya, so that when the believer repeats it and then goes out into life, he walks in it according to the Christian calling.

4.3.0.en: All the believers form the one body of Christ, and in the body of Christ the Holy Spirit is the giver of life to all the members, and all the believers have one hope, that to which God has called us, which is the hope of the second coming of Christ.

4.4.0.en: The head of this body is the Lord Christ, and He is one King over the hearts of all. We all confess faith in Jesus Christ as Redeemer, Lord and God, since we have entered by Baptism into one covenant with Christ and with one another, by our unity in the Church.

4.5.0.en: Of all: this one God and Father cares for all His creatures, even if they deny Him. Above all: that is, the possessor of authority and lordship over all His creation.

4.5.1.en: Through all: He works through all, and His fatherhood appears in their lives, so they glorify Him.

4.5.2.en: We believe in one God and not in many different gods like the pagan Gentiles, and we do not look on Him in a spirit of bondage and fear as Judaism looked on Him in the Old Testament, but, receiving the spirit of adoption, we call Him Father and trust in His care for us and His shepherding of us.

4.5.3.en: Thus unity is achieved among the Christian denominations and confessions if they are based on one faith, one Baptism and one creed. Let us all pray for this, so that all may return to the one faith and the one Church.

4.6.s.en: (2) The gifts of the Holy Spirit

4.6.0.en: The unity of the Church does not prevent the gifts given to her members from being different. To each member a gift has been given, so that none of the members is left without a gift. The spiritual gifts are one in their origin, that is, their source, but varied in their forms, and the Lord Jesus has given to each one of the believers according to the measure or extent that He willed for him.

4.7.0.en: The Apostle quoted this verse from (Ps 68:18) and took it as a prophecy of the victory of Christ at His ascension after He accomplished redemption on the Cross.

4.7.1.en: Led captivity captive: Christ triumphed over death by His death and resurrection, and over him who has the power of death, that is, Satan.

4.7.2.en: The people whom Satan had taken captive and who lived in hell, Christ snatched from this enemy, set free and redeemed by His grace and made His people, so they became captives of Christ, as the Apostle said of himself that he was "the prisoner of the Lord" (v. 1). Gave gifts: Christ, the conqueror who takes the many spoils of His victories, is able to enrich His soldiers with many gifts of the gifts and fruits of the Holy Spirit.

4.8.0.en: Christ descended into hell through the Cross and brought out the spirits of the believers of the Old Testament who were in the grip of the devil.

4.9.0.en: That Christ ascended implies that He descended; that is, He who came down to earth and took our nature is the one who ascended to the highest possible place, above all beings, visible and invisible. We cannot grasp the loftiness of the exaltation to which God raised Him, that He might fill all with the fruits and gifts of the Holy Spirit ... This is the saving work of the Lord for the believers.

4.10.0.en: The Holy Spirit, who was poured out on the day of Pentecost, granted varied gifts and different endowments to the believers, so He gave some to be:

4.10.1.en: Apostles: those whom Christ chose to preach to the whole creation.

4.10.2.en: Prophets: not only those who foretell the future, but prophecy in the New Testament means speaking about our future, which is eternal life, so the meaning of prophets is those who teach the spiritual life and prepare people for the Kingdom.

4.10.3.en: Evangelists: those who go about proclaiming the Gospel, like Philip (Acts 8). Pastors: those whom the Lord appoints to shepherd the congregations or local churches. Pastors can be teachers, whether bishops and priests or members of the Church.

4.11.0.en: This variety of gifts achieves completeness of knowledge, holiness and love for the believers in the Church, for these gifts complete the ministry to the believers in the Church so that they grow in the love of Christ and in knowing Him.

4.12.0.en: A perfect man: the Christian perfection that we are required to strive toward.

4.12.1.en: The measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ: our measure of perfection is Christ, so we strive toward Him to reach as much perfection as we can, not the absolute perfection of Christ. We do not compare ourselves with others, but our only highest example is Christ. We learn from all the saints, but our striving is toward Christ.

4.12.2.en: God's will is that we grow and go deeper in the knowledge of Christ until we come to the unity of the faith, so that we know the Lord Jesus with increasing knowledge, that He may be our only goal and the joy of our hearts. In this way the members of the Church and her shepherds join together for the success of the Lord's work without division among themselves.

4.12.3.en: God gives gifts to all His children in the Church, so try to know your abilities and gifts, and know that they were given to you so that you use them in the service of the Church. A gift is not a proof of your goodness, but using it faithfully increases your love toward God and benefits others, so God rejoices and blesses you.

4.13.0.en: God does not want the believers to be like little children who have no stability or steadfastness, so that they are exposed to being deceived by the trickery and cunning of false teachers in order to achieve their malicious ends.

4.14.0.en: Let us stand firm in God's truth declared in His Gospel, confessing Him and loving Him, showing love to those who have strayed from Him, warning them gently and with a desire for the salvation of their souls, so that we reach spiritual maturity and grow in our spiritual life, imitating Christ the head of the Church.

4.14.1.en: Among the most important means that protect us from the misleading teachings proclaimed by some who have departed from the Church are studying the Holy Bible in a spirit of prayer and the interpretation of the Fathers of the Church. May we take care to read the Holy Bible every day and to attend the meetings and liturgies of the Church, and not accept teaching from anyone outside the Church, even if it seems dazzling.

4.15.0.en: According to the effectual working in the measure of every part: every believer in the Church, whether his work is small or great, grows in the love of God, and by this growth, which sometimes seems small because this person's work is small, growth takes place for the whole body, that is, the Church.

4.15.1.en: The Church, composed of many believing members, is like the human body, composed of many members joined together and united. Every joint in it is a living member that contributes to the life of the whole body according to its function and its role in giving life to the body. The spiritual power that each member of the Church receives from Christ is a source of life for the whole Church, and the Church's growth in the likeness of Christ requires that she be full of love and all her members be united with Christ the Head and with one another.

4.16.0.en: The Apostle, who speaks by the Spirit of God, entreats the believers not to walk as the rest of the Gentiles walk, who walk in evil and defilement, led in that by their reprobate mind, deceived by evil.

4.17.0.en: The wretched souls far from God are separated from Him and have no spiritual life, because of the hardness and blindness of their hearts, and their minds are darkened because they are empty of God's light. And because their owners persist in evil, they are ignorant and refuse to know God.

4.18.0.en: The wicked Gentiles, whose consciences have died and no longer rebuke them for the evil of their deeds, commit unchaste sins without concern and without fear of God. Rather they go on in works of uncleanness and fornication with greediness and covetousness, and so they corrupt themselves.

4.19.0.en: Your knowledge of Christ, O believers, and of His principles and His life, and your experience of His power, which worked to renew your minds, this knowledge does not allow you to walk like the Gentiles in evil.

4.20.0.en: You have heard the voice of Christ, and hearing here is obedience of the heart and not merely hearing with the ear, and your hearing His voice requires of you not to walk like the Gentiles but by the commandments of Christ, that is, His truth.

4.21.0.en: The old man: the nature in man inclined to evil before Baptism, which dies in it, and man is born with a new nature inclined to good.

4.21.1.en: The Apostle calls the believers to reject their former evil works, in whose lusts they were immersed, and, instead of repenting, were filled with pride.

4.22.0.en: The spirit of your mind: the human spirit, which includes his mind and heart, and which the Holy Spirit renews.

4.22.1.en: The renewal of the believers takes place by their receiving the new nature in the sacrament of Baptism, and this renewal continues through the sacrament of repentance and confession. Renewal takes place first in thought, so that works become pure, befitting the children of God, and all this by the work of the Holy Spirit.

4.23.0.en: In Baptism we receive the new nature, which is inclined to be like God and to do good and righteousness and all works of holiness.

4.23.1.en: May you occupy your mind with prayer, spiritual reading and meditation, so that your life is changed by the power of the Holy Spirit who dwells in you, and you drive out the love of sin with the love of God's word and conversation with Him, and you incline to cling to the children of God and share with them in works of mercy.

4.24.s.en: (4) Leaving sins and holding fast to love of others

4.24.0.en: It befits the new man, created according to the will of God in righteousness and holiness, to be faithful and truthful in his works and in his words, and to leave lying so as not to deceive the other believers, because we are all members of one body, so none can deceive another without harming the whole body. Some may justify the sin of lying or divide it into kinds, but all of it is a great sin that keeps us from entering the Kingdom (Rev 21:8, Col 3:9).

4.25.0.en: Right anger is firmness for the good of the other and is joined with love, but in wrong anger a person loses his inner peace and it is accompanied by sins such as weak love toward others, even resentment, and it may appear in words painful to people or harmful actions. Paul continues his discourse, warning us that if we fall into wrong anger we should not continue in it, but forgive and reconcile with others before the sun goes down, that is, before the day ends, so that we regain our peace and the peace of those around us by apologizing and restoring understanding and love.

4.26.0.en: If we keep some anger in our hearts, we thereby give the enemy of good an opening to enter our life and dominate it, so that he robs us of our joys, changes our relationship with people and fills us with malice.

4.27.0.en: The Apostle warns the one who falls into the sin of stealing, through his selfishness, weak love for others and laziness, to rise and work with his hands, not only to meet his own needs but to turn to giving and meeting the needs of the needy. Thus we see Christianity transforming man from selfishness to giving.

4.28.0.en: The warning here is against bad speech and the urging is toward good speech. The bad word is what stirs up unclean thought and leads to evil works, while good speech is what is beneficial to the hearers and contains teaching, advice and guidance, so that the content of the speech is according to the needs of the hearer, to give him spiritual benefit according to his need.

4.29.0.en: The day of redemption: the second coming of Christ.

4.29.1.en: Evil conduct and bad words grieve the Spirit of God who dwells within the believers. This ought not to happen, because our members have been sealed by the Holy Spirit in the sacrament of the Holy Myron to be set apart for Him, and we live for righteousness until the end of our life, to receive salvation and the complete redemption of Christ when He brings us into the eternal Kingdom.

4.30.0.en: Bitterness: evil and distress within man.

4.30.2.en: Let not harshness of character, which makes a person quick to anger, be among your qualities, and put away from you every inner feeling of distress, grumbling and discontent, which appears in the form of wrath, that is, intense anger full of cunning and evil and accompanied by clamor.

4.31.0.en: Kindness is one of the fruits of the Holy Spirit, and our being kind to one another is a proof of our love. Our compassion and forgiveness toward others is a proof of our imitating Christ, for as God forgave us our sins and pardoned us and had compassion on us in the face of eternal destruction, so we must forgive our brethren.

4.31.1.en: Perhaps we think that if someone wrongs us he does not deserve our forgiveness. Do we then ask ourselves whether we were worthy of divine forgiveness?? ... However much someone wrongs you, he cannot reach the degree to which you have sinned against God, and yet He loved you and forgave you and all of us all our sins. Have you reviewed your attitude toward the one who has wronged you?!

4.31.2.en: Do not think about how much evil he has done, but about the measure of God's love for you in His forgiving you. Forgive the one who has wronged you for God's sake, and even pray for him, because sin is weakness and we are all liable to weakness, so support him with your prayers.
